3) Life Jacket: Mr. Staples was not wearing a life jacket at the time of his fall overboard.
Had he been wearing a Coast Guard approved life jacket, he may have remained afloat to
be safely rescued.
4. There is no evidence of misconduct, inattention to duty, or negligent or willful violation of law or
regulation on the part of American Cruise Lines, Inc., licensed or certificated personnel, or Coast Guard
personnel.
5. There is no evidence of failure to properly respond to this situation by American Cruise Lines, Inc.,
the crew of the Passenger Vessel QUEEN OF THE WEST, the U. S. Coast Guard or any other
responsible agency.
6. There is no evidence that any personnel of the Coast Guard or of any other agency or any other person
contributed to this casualty.
Recommendations:
Safety
1. Recommend that the Commandant of the Coast Guard consider requiring life rings with lights on both
sides of the main deck and searchlights in rescue boats as part of Subchapter K Regulations.
2. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. test random crew members in Man Overboard
drills annually. Coast Guard Marine Inspectors should plan to conduct a scheduled drill with the crew at
the earliest convenience to the vessel after all temporary summer employees and deckhands have been
hired and have had a chance to become familiar with the vessel.
3. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. develop an inclusive safety policy with regard to
all crew wearing life jackets while working in the vicinity of the stern. American Cruise Lines, Inc.
should consider required personal protective equipment, safety practices, buddy system, and/or tie-off
system in developing their policy.
4. It is recommended that American Cruise Lines, Inc. assign all crew members a duty during a man
overboard event and document these duties on the Station Bill.
